# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_013_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 5

**1** After completing the writing as directed in the earlier vision, the Spirit of God lifted me up and transported me to a wild, pathless region. **2** In an instant the Spirit shifted, and my vision cleared — I could see the tower plainly, and around it stood twelve mountains, each one completely distinct. **3** The first mountain was black as soot. The second was bare rock — nothing grew on it. The third was choked with thorns and briars. The fourth had some vegetation — parts green, parts withered at the top. The fifth had green grass but was rough and rocky. The sixth was riddled with cracks and crevices, large and small. The seventh was cheerful and lush — teeming with life. Animals and birds of all kinds fed on it, and the more they ate the more it grew. The eighth was dotted with springs of fresh water, and every creature God had made came there to drink. **4** The ninth was a stark wilderness — no water anywhere — inhabited by savage beasts and venomous serpents that killed people who came near. The tenth had enormous trees casting deep shade; flocks of sheep rested there and grazed peacefully. The eleventh was covered in dense trees loaded with every kind of fruit; whoever tasted it wanted more. The twelfth mountain was entirely white, brilliant and joyful to look at.

---

*PNEUMA note: The twelve mountains form a moral panorama of the Church — from the darkest apostates to the purest martyrs. The movement from black to white is a journey from death toward eschatological holiness.*
